chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrour (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Aamir narrated from his uncle Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umair, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the Truthful One, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said:
Religion is null for one who has no taqiyah (piety/concealment), and faith is null for one who lacks wara' (piety/deduction).

key_terms.تَقِيَّة: Taqiyah: Piety, or the practice of concealing one's faith/beliefs in times of danger; also interpreted as general piety in this context.
key_terms.دِين: Deen: Religion, faith, or way of life.
key_terms.وَرَعَ: Wara': Scrupulousness, piety, or carefulness in avoiding the doubtful and the forbidden.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'la deena liman la taqiyyata lahu' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes *taqiyah* not merely as political dissimulation but as a fundamental pillar of religious validity, reflecting the Shia experience under Umayyad and Abbasid pressures. He pairs this with *wara'* (scrupulousness), indicating that true faith requires both the protective wisdom of concealment and the ethical rigor of avoiding doubtful matters. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for understanding the dual nature of Shia identity: outward adaptability and inward purity.
